data.long_meaning: From the Latin 'laborans montis', meaning 'one who toils on the mountain'. This name was given to a young warrior or one who labors and struggles towards a goal. The name Lamont carries the meaning “Young warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lamont usually hope their child will grow to embody young warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Lamont, a Scottish clan with origins dating back to the 13th century. The name is believed to have derived from the Gaelic 'lamh mhonaidh' which means 'long monk'. The Lamonts were a powerful and influential clan, who held significant lands in the Scottish Borders and were important players in the political landscape of the region. They were historically associated with the English border marches and had strong ties with both the Scottish and English monarchies.

Lamont, a French-Canadian surname. The name is believed to have originated from the French 'l'homme montant', meaning 'the mountaineer'. The name was given to settlers who lived in the mountainous regions of Canada, particularly in the province of Quebec. These settlers were often of French origin, but also included Irish, Scottish, and other European immigrants. The name became common among the French-Canadian population and is still found in Quebec and other parts of Canada today.
